title: [CRY-12] Client-side rejection of valid Commits has no fork semantics; the DM consent model is not
description: Review finding CRY-12: Client-side rejection of valid Commits has no fork semantics; the DM consent model is not implementable in MLS (lens CRY). Location: spec/04-access-control.md:159, spec/04-access-control.md:103. Fix: 04:159 says "The Add is not committed until a configurable consent threshold of existing members issues a matching Commit". One Commit per epoch makes "a threshold of matching Commits" impossible. The alternative "or explicit approval signal" is undefined. 04:103 says "Clients MUST reject a Commit that adds a DID with a standing `BanRecord`". Under RFC 9420 §14, a member that refuses the canonical Commit is left on a dead branch, and the spec gives no next step. Fix as proposed: define the approval signal as signed application messages that must precede the Commit, and define the reaction to a policy-violating Commit (leave, alert the user, recreate the group). The location 04:78 in CRY.md is not affected, because it constrains a joiner before it has any state. Full text: notes/review/CRY-verified.md and notes/review/CRY.md.
